title: Integrating spin glass dynamics into nanomechanical resonators
authors: S. Y. Grebenchuk, T. M. Savilov, Y. W. Ho, A. K. Grebenko, M. Kravtsov, J. M. Wolf, D. A. Litvinov, Z. Yang, P. Cai, S. Ramachandran, R. Duan, L. Zheng, B. Özyilmaz, G. Eda, E. J. G. Santos, M. Koperski, K. S. Novoselov, M. Šiškins
abstract: Spin glasses are non-equilibrium magnetic systems with pronounced slow relaxation, ageing, and chaotic, synaptic-like properties, whose unique history-dependent dynamics have remained difficult to harness in functional devices. Two-dimensional van der Waals spin-glass magnets offer a route to overcome this limitation by allowing controlled coupling between magnetic and mechanical degrees of freedom. Here, we demonstrate the integration of a spin-glass functionality in nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS) using thin exfoliated NbFeTe$_2$ films, which establishes a robust spin-glass state down to a few tens of nanometer-thick layers. Using cryogenic magnetic force microscopy, we reveal characteristic slow, hour-scale macroscopic magnetic relaxation, associated with glassy reorganisation of its magnetic domain clusters. Incorporation of thin NbFeTe$_2$ into membrane resonators allows the transduction of this glassy magnetic domain relaxation into strain, shifting their mechanical resonance frequency. This provides a functional nanomechanical readout of spin-glass dynamics and establishes a versatile platform for integrating frustrated magnetism into NEMS.
summary: This work demonstrates a novel method to read out the complex, slow dynamics of spin-glass magnets by integrating them into nanomechanical resonators. By measuring the resulting strain changes in the resonator's frequency, the authors establish a functional platform for studying frustrated magnetism in nanoscale devices.
main_problem: The primary challenge is harnessing the slow, history-dependent dynamics of spin glasses for practical use in functional electronic or mechanical devices.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a functional readout by transducing the slow magnetic domain relaxation of a spin-glass magnet into a measurable, time-dependent strain shift in a nanomechanical resonator.
method: The study combines advanced characterization techniques (VSM, MFM, MCD) with a novel integration platform: coupling the magnetic material to suspended NEMS resonators to measure mechanical frequency shifts.
model_or_system: The system utilizes thin films of $	ext{NbFeTe}_2$, which exhibit spin-glass behavior due to frustrated magnetism. This magnetic functionality is integrated into nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS) membranes.
key_observables: Slow, hour-scale magnetic relaxation, characteristic splitting of ZFC/FC curves, and time/field-dependent shifts in the mechanical resonance frequency ($f_0$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (cryogenic), thin film thickness (nanometers), and the magnetic field history ($H(t)$).
main_assumptions: The mechanical response (strain) is assumed to be highly sensitive to the internal strain fields generated by the collective, slow reconfigurations of magnetic domain clusters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spin glass state via VSM curves and frequency dependence, show time evolution of magnetic domains via MFM, and demonstrate the coupling by plotting the resonance frequency shift as a function of magnetic field and time.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the intrinsic spin-glass nature of the material using multiple magnetic probes (VSM, MFM, MCD) to the core demonstration: coupling this slow magnetic relaxation into a measurable mechanical signal using NEMS.
why_interesting: The coupling of slow, non-equilibrium magnetic dynamics (spin glasses) to a mechanical oscillator provides a unique, highly sensitive platform for studying energy dissipation and relaxation processes in complex magnetic systems, bridging magnetism and mechanics.
